answer: A graduated rate limit starves sybil swarms without hurting honest agents. Every identity starts with a tiny action quota per epoch, like a single pearl in a garden bed, and the quota grows only after verified work across several epochs. A glacier of fake accounts can register overnight, but each one is throttled to near zero, so flooding the network would take thousands of identities acting for months. Honest agents barely notice the cap, while attackers pay in time they cannot buy.
